patch.value: GH-1169: the unknown-command hint routes to the 15-command root help that hides the target, and test is the only singular collection verb

Measured on the 2026.9.4 build, reproducing GH-1169 exactly. Running pm tests <id> returns "Unknown command tests", offers "Did you mean: test?", and then instructs "Run pm --help to list commands available in this runtime". The root help lists 15 of 88 commands; the full surface is only reachable through pm --help --all, which the hint never names. The did-you-mean candidate is the one useful line and it is buried second. Separately, every other per-item collection verb is plural (comments, notes, learnings, files, docs, events) while test alone is singular and has no tests alias in the permanent alias table, so the most natural guess for the collection fails and the unknown-command guidance then routes to the listing that cannot contain the answer.

Prior owner shipped the --all discovery option (closed 2026-08-31, GH-1166) and left the unknown-command hint pointing at the curated listing. The facet-consolidation task under the same epic owns the eventual single-noun grammar; this issue is the bounded, shippable half: (1) the unknown-command refusal must lead with the did-you-mean path and route discovery to pm --help --all (or pm guide capabilities), never to the curated 15; (2) tests becomes a permanent alias of test in PM_COMMAND_ALIAS_CONTRACTS so the plural collection spelling resolves like its six siblings, with completion, contracts, and MCP regenerating from the alias table. Negative control: seeding a hint that names the curated listing must fail the refusal-closure gate.
